scout.purpose: Every coroutine needs a parent whose lifetime, completion, failure, and cancellation make concurrent work understandable and bounded.
scout.realWorldUse: Screen loading, repository operations, parallel requests, and app-scoped caches all need explicit owners rather than detached background jobs.
scout.outcome: Choose launch, async, coroutineScope, and an owner scope while preserving parent-child completion and failure.

sections.title: A CoroutineScope combines context and lifetime

blocks.text: CoroutineScope provides a CoroutineContext containing a Job and dispatcher. launch returns a Job for work whose result is observed through state or side effects; async returns Deferred and should represent a value that will be awaited. Builders inherit context and create child jobs. GlobalScope has application-like lifetime without structured ownership and is almost never appropriate for app feature work. Android supplies lifecycleScope and viewModelScope; repositories may receive a longer-lived external scope only for operations that truly must outlive a caller.

blocks.caption: Independent children share one operation lifetime and both complete before it returns.

blocks.title: Builder contract
rows: Deferred value that will be awaited

blocks.text: coroutineScope is a suspending boundary that waits for all children and fails when a child fails. It is useful for parallel decomposition inside one operation. async does not make work concurrent until it is started, and concurrency is useful only for independent operations. Awaiting immediately after each async serialises them. A suspend function should normally expose its result rather than launch hidden work; the caller can then decide lifecycle, cancellation, timeout, and error handling.

blocks.caption: Independent children share one operation lifetime and both complete before it returns.

blocks.title: Every coroutine has an owner
blocks.text: A job tree should reveal who waits, cancels, and handles failure.

sections.title: Structured children cannot outlive their operation accidentally

blocks.text: Structured concurrency means children complete before the parent operation returns, cancellation flows down, and failure has defined propagation. Long-lived work must have an explicitly injected owner and documented reason. App-visible work that must survive process death needs WorkManager rather than an in-memory scope. During review, draw the job tree and ask what cancels every node. If the answer is nobody or process termination, the lifecycle is probably accidental.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

blocks.title: Do not hide launch in suspend APIs
blocks.text: Detached work returns before completion and steals lifecycle control from the caller.

inspect.title: Find the unstructured repository launch
walkthrough: The suspend function returns before the write and provides no completion result.
GlobalScope is not cancelled by the caller and failures lack an owner.
Perform the write directly or use a documented external scope when it intentionally outlives the screen.
inspect.expectedOutput: The caller can await, cancel, and observe the bookmark result under a defined lifetime.

trap_check.mistake: Calling async and await before creating the second async child.
trap_check.why: The first result completes before the next starts, so work is sequential.
trap_check.fix: Create independent Deferred children before awaiting them.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Load two independent dashboard sources concurrently, one dependent source sequentially, and prove completion, cancellation, and failure through the job tree.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Only independent operations overlap. Caller cancellation stops every child. No coroutine uses an ownerless global scope.

recall.answer: It waits for its structured children before returning.
